summary: Somerset County fire tower in Dolebrook Township; FFLA lists it standing with cab in place, but a 2025 Forest Society of Maine newsletter describes remnants. No build date found.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing with no missing cab, but Forest Society of Maine (Fall 2025) describes remnants of fire lookout towers on Green Mountain; the sources disagree.

events.note: Forest Society of Maine newsletter describes remnants of fire lookout towers on Green Mountain, which conflicts with the FFLA listing of a standing tower.

evidence.supports: Timberland owners began building towers within two years of the 1903 fires; the state took them over by 1909
evidence.quote: Within two years of those fires, a group of timberland owners in Maine began building elevated observation towers on their properties, and by 1909, the state took over those privately funded lookouts

evidence.supports: Network of more than 100 towers, connected by telephone, each staffed by a lone observer
evidence.quote: Perched along mountainsides and ridges, Maine’s network of more than 100 fire towers was connected by telephone and staffed by lone observers who scanned the tree line for smoke and flames.

evidence.supports: Maine held out longer than most and ended its network after a 1991 budget crisis
evidence.quote: Maine held out for longer than most, discontinuing its network following a budget crisis in 1991.

evidence.supports: After the staffed system ended, some towers were dismantled or collapsed and some found a second life
evidence.quote: After the state ended its staffed fire tower system, some of the towers were dismantled or collapsed on their own and some have found a second life.

evidence.supports: Towers were built to help private landowners protect valuable trees
evidence.quote: Fire towers were built as a means for private landowners to protect the valuable trees on

evidence.supports: Towers were most numerous in Maine between 1930 and 1950
evidence.quote: by fire wardens and were most numerous in Maine between 1930 and 1950.

evidence.supports: Remnants of fire lookout towers on Green Mountain, which is part of Forest Society of Maine easements
evidence.quote: Remnants of fire lookout towers can be found on Green Mountain, #5 Mountain, #4 Mountain, and Big Spencer Mountain, all of which are part of FSM easements.

evidence.supports: Forest fires burned more than 200,000 acres in 1903, which led to the lookouts
evidence.quote: after forest fires burned more than 200,000 acres in 1903

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on current state: FFLA lists Tower Standing with no asterisk (cab in place), while the FSM newsletter (Fall 2025) says remnants of fire lookout towers remain on Green Mountain. The story reports both and does not choose. Unverified leads, not used: an FFLA Maine chapter Facebook post (seen only as a search result, never opened) says the tower was erected in 1920 and was 48 feet tall with a cab in poor shape; a second post names a watchman for 1971-1981. Check both before using. Do not confuse with the New Hampshire Green Mountain lookout on NHLR (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/nh/green-mountain-lookout/), a different tower. No access, visit or staffing data found; those keys are left unset.
